name: dispatch-pilot
description: Dispatch Pilot: a decision model outside Claude (Jev or Clef, your choice) picks the main agent's reasoning effort each time you send a message, sets it on every request of the turn, and decides it again every few steps while the turn runs. The main agent's model never changes, so the prompt cache survives. It also keeps the full skill listing out of the main agent's context and suggests the few skills that fit each message.

decisionModel.title: Decision model
decisionModel.description: Which model makes the decisions: jev (TypeSafe; needs the TypeSafe API key) or clef (Cloudflare Workers AI; needs the Cloudflare account ID and API token). The other is never used as a fallback: when the chosen one fails, the message goes on unrouted. Clef answers more slowly than Jev, so raise the decision timeout (about 3000 ms) when you choose it.

typesafeApiKey.title: TypeSafe API key
typesafeApiKey.description: Key for TypeSafe's System One API, where Jev runs (used when the decision model is jev). Without one, nothing is sent and every turn keeps the session's effort.

cloudflareAccountId.title: Cloudflare account ID
cloudflareAccountId.description: The Cloudflare account that runs Workers AI (used when the decision model is clef). It is part of the request address, which Claude Code's debug log records. Without it, nothing is sent and every turn keeps the session's effort.

cloudflareApiToken.title: Cloudflare Workers AI API token
cloudflareApiToken.description: A Cloudflare API token that can run Workers AI (used when the decision model is clef): in the dashboard, Workers AI, Use REST API, Create a Workers AI API Token. Without one, nothing is sent and every turn keeps the session's effort.

timeoutMs.title: Decision timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.description: How long a message waits for the decision model (200 to 8000). Past it the message goes on unrouted, at the session's effort, and the status line says so. Clef answers more slowly than Jev (a first request often takes 1.5 s or more): about 3000 suits it.

contextMessages.title: Recent messages sent
contextMessages.description: How many recent messages the decision model reads beside yours (0 to 32): their text and the names of the tools they called, never file contents or tool output, secrets masked.

contextTokens.title: Context budget (tokens)
contextTokens.description: How many tokens your message and the recent messages may take together (100 to 16000), counted the same way for Chinese and English; older messages are dropped first.

thetaMax.title: Threshold for max effort
thetaMax.description: The main agent goes to max only when the decision model gives max at least this probability (0 to 1); otherwise it gets the most likely of the other levels.

rejudgeEvery.title: Re-decide effort every N steps
rejudgeEvery.description: While a turn runs, the main agent's effort is decided again at every Nth step (0 to 50; 0 turns this off). Dispatching an agent, starting a Workflow or loading a skill also re-decides it.

thetaUp.title: Threshold to raise effort mid-turn
thetaUp.description: A re-decision raises the effort only when the decision model's confidence is at least this (0 to 1).

thetaDown.title: Threshold to lower effort mid-turn
thetaDown.description: A re-decision lowers the effort, by one level at most, only when the decision model's confidence is at least this (0 to 1; never below the raise threshold).

holdSteps.title: Steps before effort may drop after a raise
holdSteps.description: After a re-decision raises the effort, it does not lower it again for this many steps (0 to 50).

rejudgeSteps.title: Recent steps read when re-deciding
rejudgeSteps.description: How many of the turn's latest steps the decision model reads when it re-decides (1 to 16): the main agent's last text and the tools it called with how each ended, never file contents or tool output, secrets masked. The context budget bounds them too.

rejudgeWaitMs.title: Wait for a late re-decision (ms)
rejudgeWaitMs.description: A re-decision is asked while a tool runs; if it is not back when the next request goes out, that request waits this long for it (0 to 2000), then keeps the effort it had and the status line says so.

agentFable.title: Let dispatched agents run on fable
agentFable.description: Adds fable to the models the decision model may choose for an agent the main agent dispatches (haiku, sonnet and opus otherwise). Fable costs more than opus. A model you name yourself in your message is used either way.

agentOverride.title: Confidence to override the main agent's model pick
agentOverride.description: When the main agent names a model for an agent it dispatches, the decision model's pick replaces it only at this confidence or above (0 to 1). A model you name yourself in your message is never replaced.

skillsMax.title: Skills suggested at most
skillsMax.description: How many skills one message gets suggested at most (0 to 10); fewer, or none, when fewer reach the relevance below.

skillsMinRelevance.title: Least relevance to suggest
skillsMinRelevance.description: The relevance a skill needs to be suggested (0 to 1): its share of the decision model's answer to which skill fits the message, against every other skill and none.

skillsShortlist.title: Skills re-read in the second stage
skillsShortlist.description: How many of the skills rated highest for a message are re-read with the opening of their instructions and judged one by one (1 to 10). The second request goes out only when some skill is rated at least 0.05, and both requests together wait at most the decision timeout.

skillsProfileModel.title: Model that writes skill profiles
skillsProfileModel.description: The model (an alias such as haiku, or a full model id) that writes each skill a short profile in English and Chinese from its SKILL.md, once per version of the file, so the decision model can match a request in either language. It runs in the background through your Claude Code login and uses your plan's usage. A new model writes every profile again.

skillsProfilesPerSession.title: Skill profiles written per session
skillsProfilesPerSession.description: How many missing skill profiles are written at most each time a session starts (0 to 500; 0 writes none). The rest wait for later sessions, so a first run with many skills spreads its cost.

skillsAlwaysListed.title: Skills always listed
skillsAlwaysListed.description: Skills the main agent keeps seeing in its skill listing, by the name the listing gives them (a synced skill with its prefix, such as anthropic-skills:pdf). Every other skill is left out of the listing and suggested only when a message needs it.

skillsNeverSuggested.title: Skills never suggested
skillsNeverSuggested.description: Skills never suggested to the main agent nor pointed out to you, by the name the listing gives them. They stay installed: the Skill tool still loads one by name.
